jurisdiction.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
jurisdiction.overview: Intergovernmental organisation of 38 member countries. Its AI Recommendation is open to non-members, so it applies to its Adherents rather than to OECD membership.

narrative.summary: The OECD's one AI-specific legal instrument is the Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted on 22 May 2019 and revised in November 2023 and May 2024. Its five principles and five policy recommendations are not legally binding, but Adherents commit to implement them. They are 50 countries (all 38 OECD Members and 12 non-members) and the European Union. The radar attaches the Recommendation to each adhering country, so it appears on their pages; country pages also show the adherence.
narrative.review_notes: The OECD Compendium of Legal Instruments was searched for AI-specific instruments and only the AI Recommendation was found; adherents and adherence dates are taken from the instrument's page. Membership (38) is taken from the same site's country list, which marks each country as a Member.

instruments.current_status: In force. Adopted by the OECD Council meeting at Ministerial level on 22 May 2019 (C(2019)34, C/MIN(2019)3/FINAL); revised by the Council on 8 November 2023 to update the definition of an 'AI system' (C(2023)151) and by the Council meeting at Ministerial level on 3 May 2024 (C/MIN(2024)16/FINAL), as stated on the OECD Compendium of Legal Instruments. OECD Recommendations 'are not legally binding' but 'represent a political commitment' by Adherents (OECD booklet of the instrument). Adherents: the 38 OECD Members, 12 non-member countries and the European Union; adherence dates for non-members as listed on the instrument page. The PDF linked is the 2023 English booklet; the current English text as amended in 2024 is on the instrument page.
instruments.summary: The first intergovernmental standard on AI. It sets five values-based principles for responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI (inclusive growth and well-being; human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability) and five recommendations for national policies and international co-operation (AI research investment, an enabling digital ecosystem and policy environment, human capacity and labour-market transition, and international co-operation). Adherents commit to promote and implement it; it is not legally binding.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Intergovernmental AI principles adhered to by 50 countries and the EU; basis for the G20 AI Principles and the G7 Hiroshima Process texts.
